transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently, and my family is really worried about my eating habits. I've only been eating very small amounts lately, so they insisted I come see a doctor.

Do you find that you are restricting your food intake because you are afraid of gaining weight or feel dissatisfied with your body shape, or is it more that you have lost your appetite due to feeling very low or overwhelmed?

It's definitely because I am terrified of gaining weight. I intentionally restrict what I eat because I need to keep my weight as low as possible. It's not that I've lost my appetite; I just can't bear the thought of getting bigger.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical health, such as missing menstrual periods or feeling unusually cold, dizzy, or weak lately?
I haven't really noticed any of those physical symptoms like missing my period or feeling cold and weak. Honestly, I'm just much more focused on my weight and making sure I don't gain any of it back.
Besides restricting your food intake, do you ever engage in other behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as exercising excessively, using laxatives, or vomiting after eating?
No, I don't do things like vomiting, taking laxatives, or exercising excessively. I just focus entirely on restricting what I eat because I am so terrified of gaining weight.

When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you see yourself as being thinner than you actually are, or do you feel that your body shape or weight has an excessive influence on how you evaluate your self-worth?
I'm not quite sure how to answer that, and I haven't really thought about my body in terms of my self-worth. I just know that I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight, and that is what I focus on.
When you look at your body in the mirror, do you perceive yourself as being overweight even though others might tell you that you are at a healthy weight or even quite thin?

Yes, my family and friends constantly tell me that I'm too thin, but I just don't see it that way when I look in the mirror. I still feel like I need to lose weight and get extremely anxious about gaining anything back. To me, I never look thin enough.
